passages.title: Passage 1
passages.instructions:
Questions 1–40

You should spend about 60 minutes on Questions 1–40, which are based on the reading passage below.
passages.body:
Universal Basic Income Trials

A Universal basic income trials distribute unconditional cash payments to individuals or households, testing whether predictable transfers reduce poverty, simplify welfare bureaucracy, and alter labour supply decisions compared with means-tested benefits imposing high effective marginal tax rates when earnings rise. Pilots in Finland, Kenya, India, and North American cities varied in generosity, duration, and universality within defined geographies, producing nuanced findings rather than single verdicts applicable everywhere. Advocates argue automation and gig precarity strengthen the case for income floors decoupled from employment status, while opponents warn of fiscal unsustainability and reduced work incentives despite mixed empirical evidence often showing modest labour responses concentrated among secondary earners and students extending education rather

B Finland's two-year experiment targeted unemployed adults with monthly payments continuing if they found work, reporting improved wellbeing and reduced stress without statistically significant employment effects at aggregate level, though sample sizes and macro conditions limited generalisation. Kenyan GiveDirectly long-term village transfers documented increased assets, entrepreneurship, and psychological wellbeing, challenging stereotypes of dependency, yet scaling to national universality raises revenue questions orders of magnitude larger than NGO budgets. Stockton's mayor-led pilot in California provided cards to low-income residents showing stable employment with some shifts to part-time pursuit of training, interpreted cautiously given short duration and philanthropic funding not replicable without tax base or monetary financing debates entering political discourse contentiously.

C Administrative simplicity appeals when replacing labyrinthine programmes requiring verification caseworkers; UBI could reduce stigma and cliff effects. However, existing in-kind services—healthcare, housing vouchers—address market failures cash alone might not solve if prices rise capturing transfers as landlords increase rents unless supply policies accompany payments. Partial basic income proposals integrate with progressive taxation recouping transfers from high earners, approximating net benefits while preserving universal point of access reducing take-up barriers seen in underclaimed entitlements due to paperwork burdens deterring eligible seniors and immigrants fearful of immigration enforcement interacting with benefit rules complexity lawyers navigate profitably while poor remain unassisted—a justice argument for simpler interfaces even if headline gross costs scare fiscal

D Macroeconomic simulations model consumption multipliers, inflationary pressures if everyone spends simultaneously without productive capacity expansion, and labour market tightening in low-wage sectors potentially raising wages beneficially or prices harmfully depending on elasticities and import competition absorbing demand. Funding options include value-added taxes, carbon dividends recycling permit revenues, sovereign wealth dividends from resource rents, and monetary financing rejected in most advanced economies fearing hyperinflation histories though proponents distinguish small predictable flows from deficit monetisation during crises already practiced opaquely via asset purchases affecting distribution unequally anyway according to heterodox critics engaging mainstream models with overlapping generations structures showing demographic transitions interact with pension systems making UBI discussions entangled with retirement reform

E Political economy constraints dominate feasibility: winners and losers from replacing programmes create veto players—landlords, social service agencies, insurers—benefiting from status quo complexity. Referendum campaigns in Switzerland and elsewhere failed though garnered minority support educating publics. Conditional cash transfers in Latin America contrast by requiring health clinic visits, blending paternalism with poverty reduction successes UBI purists reject philosophically yet pragmatic progressives admire for measurable child health outcomes. Indigenous revenue-sharing proposals resemble partial UBIs from territorial rights, linking debates to colonial restitution not only technocratic poverty lines statistical agencies update periodically without capturing culturally specific notions of sufficiency community assemblies articulate in deliberations increasingly influencing regional policy experiments bypassing national gridlock when

F Behavioural responses include financial literacy needs; lump sums poorly managed may dissipate without banking access and scam protections. Mental health improvements documented in several pilots could reduce healthcare costs offsetting part of expenditure dynamically ignored in static costings. Gender impacts may empower women in patriarchal households gaining independent income, though risk of intra-household conflict requires safeguarding research ethically. Disability advocates worry UBI could justify cutting specialised supports if politicians treat one-size payments as replacement rather than floor, a coalition fracture UBI movements must address explicitly pledging supplemental services intact—a strategic communication challenge when fiscal conservatives court UBI rhetoric to streamline cuts cynically, prompting progressive advocates to insist on net expansion

G Looking ahead, the author believes trials remain valuable for local learning but national adoption requires durable funding and housing alignment. UBI is neither panacea nor poison; context determines outcomes. Combining modest universal payments with robust public services and pro-worker labour law may reduce precarity more than cash alone. If pilots remain philanthropic short-term, they risk becoming publicity stunts not policy blueprints. Transparent evaluation, participant voice, and integration with tax policy distinguish serious experimentation from slogans. Democracies facing inequality may revisit income floors as technology and climate transitions disrupt livelihoods, provided debates confront power structures not only calculator spreadsheets estimating break-even GDP growth assumptions sensitive to modeller choices often opaque to
